content:
sam: Quick idea — add a new deploy-bot subcommand `deploy preview` that spins an ephemeral preflight env, runs smoke checks, and emits a ready-to-paste release-note snippet for change windows. Brain dump below.

olga: What's the main diff vs `dry-run`?

sam: Dry-run validates manifests and lints templates. Preview should actually create a short-lived staging slice (configurable TTL), run the smoke suite, collect latency/errors, and output a structured summary + markdown release-note draft.

ryan: Sounds useful but potentially costly. Can we make flags to limit scope? e.g. `--manifest-only`, `--notes-only`, or `--no-ephemeral` to only run local checks. Example: `/deploy preview --manifest --notes-only`

maya: Auto notes are 👍. Can we also include suggested rollback lines (so SREs or PMs can paste into Jira)? Example output idea:

```
Preview report (preview-1782233344):
- Services touched: api, runtime-worker
- DB migrations: none
- Smoke tests: 18/18 passed
- Performance delta: +12ms p95 on api
- Flags: quantized-model=v1.3 (pinned)

Suggested rollback commands:
  - deploy rollback api --to-tag=2024-03-12T03:21Z
  - deploy rollback runtime-worker --to-tag=2024-03-12T03:19Z

Release note (markdown):
- Feature: support pinned model v1.3 for cost/perf balance
- Risk: small p95 latency regression (12ms) in api; monitor for 30m after rollout
- Change window: 2024-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC
```

deploy-bot: mocked: created preview env `preview-1782233344-1` (ttl=10m). smoke: OK. artifacts: /tmp/preview-1782233344/report.json :eyes:

sam: Also add a `--change-window` flag so the bot stamps timezone-aware windows into notes (`--change-window=\"2024-03-14T02:00/2024-03-14T04:00Z\"`). That helps automated Jira comment/Slack post.

ryan: Also a `--pin-version` flag to surface any pinned model or runtime versions used during preview (reduces surprise rollouts). `/deploy preview --pin-version model:v1.3`

olga: I'll hack together a tiny generator to turn the preview report into the release-note template. prototype (python):

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json,sys
r=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
md = [f"- Services: {', '.join(r['services'])}", f"- Risk: {r.get('risk','none')}", f"- Smoke: {r['smoke_passed']}/ {r['smoke_total']}"]
print("Release note (auto):\\n" + "\\n".join(md))
```

maya: Sg. Can we keep the canonical template in the repo at `.deploy/templates/release_note.md` with placeholders like `{{services}}`, `{{risk}}`, `{{rollback_cmds}}` so the bot just fills them?

sam: Yes — next steps: olga to open PR adding `deploy preview` handler + unit tests and a small integration test that runs with `--no-ephemeral`. ryan to draft cost/runbook and parameter limits (max 3 previews/hour per team). I'll add a short section to the release playbook.

infra-bot: Reminder: per policy, production change windows > 1% of traffic require 24h notice and runbook linked. See `#policy-change-windows` for details.

ryan: tagging prod oncall FYI @maya — would you be okay being the backup reviewer for the initial rollout? :shipit:

maya: happy to. please add a small smoke-run dashboard link to the preview output so oncall can glance quickly.

sam: Nice — keeping it simple and optional flags should make adoption low-friction. I'll sketch the CLI UX and endpoint payloads tomorrow and drop them in the PR description.
